Definition: to sow; figuratively, to disseminate, plant, fructify
BiblicalUsage: Zara is the ordinary word for sowing seed, and the Bible uses it from the first chapter of Genesis, where the earth brings forth plants yielding seed, to the farmer who sows in the morning and does not hold back his hand in the evening. It also carries the darker side of sowing: Hosea warns that those who sow the wind will reap the whirlwind, and the seed a person plants decides the harvest. In the Psalms the same word turns to hope, as those who sow in tears reap in joy.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe sowing is one of the clearest pictures in Scripture of how God works, because the harvest never lies about the seed. We cannot sow carelessness and expect faithfulness to grow, and we cannot sow generously and expect God to forget it. My position is simple: plant what is true, plant it early, and trust God with the increase.
